objective: Measure smoke particle size distributions from overheated spacecraft materials and evaluate ionization and photoelectric smoke detector performance in microgravity.
fuel: Teflon, Kapton, silicone rubber, cellulose, dibutyl-phthalate on porous wick
key_finding: All samples produced significant sub-micron particulate better detected by ionization detectors, though a light scattering detector would perform well in most cases. Silicone rubber AMD was 227 nm but almost half the particle mass was larger than 1000 nm.
quote: Overall, 30 samples were tested comprising of six samples each of ﬁve different materials: TeﬂonTM, KaptonTM, silicone rubber, cellulose, and dibutyl-phthalate (a chemical used to make ﬂexible plastic) deposited on a porous wick.
source_title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME) — NASA summary

objective: Compare flight and ground smoke particle size distributions from SAME-2 materials and evaluate ISS and Shuttle smoke detectors.
fuel: Teflon, Kapton, cotton, silicone rubber, Pyrell
measurements: thermal precipitator with TEM, aerosol instruments (moments of size distribution), commercial smoke detector, ISS and Shuttle smoke detectors; SMPS on ground
key_finding: Flight moment measurements were compared with ground SMPS size distributions and TEM analysis for un-aged and aged smoke to check lognormal assumptions.
quote: The Re-ﬂight of the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME-2) was conducted during Expedition 24 (July – September 2010) and ﬂight experiment results have been analyzed with respect to comparable ground-based experiment results.
source_title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME) — NASA summary

hardware: Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) gas burner in drop rig
objective: Verify that a gaseous-fuel burner (BRE) with 25 mm and 50 mm diameters can emulate condensed-fuel flames in microgravity, and examine how pressure, O2 and flow rate affect heat of gasification.
sample_geometry: circular porous burner, 25 mm and 50 mm diameter
measurements: heat flux sensor, heat flux sensor temperature, outlet plate thermocouples (center and offset radius R*), fuel mass flow rate, flame images for flame height
key_finding: Nominally hemispherical flame with decelerating growth and quasi-steady heat flux after about 5 s; flame height reached only about 37% of steady state in the 25 mm example. Burning rate was higher than theory for the 50 mm burner, which indicates significant gas radiation.
quote: The microgravity results exhibit a nominally hemispherical flame with decelerating growth and quasi-steady heat flux after about 5 seconds.
source_title: Emulation of Condensed Fuel Flames Using a Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) in Microgravity

hardware: Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) gas burner in drop rig
objective: Determine the effect of ambient pressure on heat of gasification for BRE flames in microgravity.
fuel: gaseous fuel (methane/ethylene), same burner and similar mass flow rates
sample_geometry: circular porous burner (25 mm or 50 mm)
measurements: heat flux, burning rate (derived heat of gasification)
key_finding: Heat of gasification increases with ambient pressure (tested range 0.5-1.0 atm), whereas the theoretical models predict no pressure dependence.
quote: Two sets of tests with 30% oxygen content are chosen to study the influence of ambient pressure on heat of gasification as can be seen in Figure 6a.
source_title: Emulation of Condensed Fuel Flames Using a Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) in Microgravity

hardware: Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) gas burner in drop rig
objective: Determine the effect of oxygen mole fraction on heat of gasification for BRE flames in microgravity.
fuel: gaseous fuel (methane/ethylene), same burner and similar mass flow rates
sample_geometry: circular porous burner (25 mm or 50 mm)
measurements: heat flux, burning rate (derived heat of gasification)
key_finding: Heat of gasification rises monotonically with oxygen content (mole fraction 0.21-0.30) at 1 atm and the same mass flow rate.
quote: The two sets of tests selected for this analysis have the same mass flow rate and 1 atm pressure. The heat of gasification shows a monotonic rise with the oxygen content.
source_title: Emulation of Condensed Fuel Flames Using a Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) in Microgravity

objective: Measure particle size of smoke from overheated Kapton at baseline flow, unaged vs aged 720 s.
sample_geometry: small sample heated by wire in smoke generation duct for ~60 s
measurements: P-Trak (M0), ionization chamber (M1), DustTrak/MPASS (M3), TEM grids
key_finding: Unaged Kapton Dg 0.042 um, count mean 0.056 um, mass diameter 0.101 um; aging 720 s raised these to 0.089, 0.109, 0.161 um (sigma_g 2.154 to 1.872).
source_title: Particle Morphology and Size Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2 (AIAA 2012-3536)

objective: Measure particle size of smoke from overheated lamp wick (cellulose), unaged vs aged 720 s.
sample_geometry: small sample heated by wire in smoke generation duct for ~60 s
key_finding: Lampwick unaged mass diameter 0.258 um rising to 0.398 um aged 720 s; large portions of particles had aerodynamic diameter >1 um.
source_title: Particle Morphology and Size Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2 (AIAA 2012-3536)

objective: Measure particle size of smoke from overheated silicone rubber, unaged vs aged 720 s.
sample_geometry: small sample heated by wire in smoke generation duct for ~60 s
key_finding: Silicone unaged mass diameter 0.465 um rising to 0.619 um aged; largest diameters among materials; no particles visible in TEM (liquid droplets evaporated).
source_title: Particle Morphology and Size Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2 (AIAA 2012-3536)

objective: Measure particle size of smoke from overheated Teflon, unaged vs aged 720 s.
sample_geometry: small sample heated by wire in smoke generation duct for ~60 s
key_finding: Teflon particles very small: mass diameter 0.170 um unaged, 0.232 um aged; solid agglomerate (fractal-like) structure.
source_title: Particle Morphology and Size Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2 (AIAA 2012-3536)

objective: Measure particle size of smoke from overheated Pyrell foam, unaged vs aged 720 s.
sample_geometry: small sample heated by wire in smoke generation duct for ~60 s
key_finding: Pyrell unaged mass diameter 0.384 um, aged 0.539 um; fractal-like clusters of up to 30 primary spheres at 8 cm/s.
source_title: Particle Morphology and Size Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2 (AIAA 2012-3536)

objective: Examine the effect of zero airflow on smoke particle size and morphology during sample heating.
key_finding: Diameter of average mass was 30-40% larger in zero-flow tests (11 tests); Pyrell smoke changed from fractal clusters to spherical particles; about half the smoke was lost via the inlet.
quote: It is found for all of the materials the diameter of average mass is 30 % to 40 % larger for the zero-flow tests compared to the flow tests.
source_title: Particle Morphology and Size Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2 (AIAA 2012-3536)

objective: Measure O2 depletion and CO/CO2 production to evaluate combustion completeness and stoichiometry of PMMA flames in microgravity under ventilation flow.
sample_geometry: rods 6.35-12.7 mm diameter, slabs 0.125-5 mm thick, section of 4 cm diameter sphere; opposed and concurrent flow
measurements: CSA-CP (O2, CO), CDM (CO2), MCA offset, thermopile radiometer, color video, still camera, air velocity transducer
key_finding: O2 consumed vs CO2 produced agreed with the 6:5 stoichiometric ratio over a range of initial O2 (~14-21%), flows and geometries. Heat release rates were mostly well below 100 W. Global equivalence ratio was ~1.3 (fuel rich).
quote: The data, taken over a wide range of initial oxygen concentrations, forced opposed or concurrent flow velocities, and using various sample geometries, is compared with this stoichiometric ratio (6O2 : 5 CO2) in Figure 5.
source_title: Results from On-Board CSA-CP and CDM Sensor Readings During the BASS-II Experiment in the MSG (ICES-2015-196)

objective: Determine the global equivalence ratio from fuel mass loss and oxygen consumption.
measurements: post-flight sample mass loss, CSA-CP and CDM before/after readings
key_finding: Observed slope of 0.4582 O2%/g fuel gave global equivalence ratio of 1.3 on average, so flames were under-ventilated and fuel rich.
quote: Using the observed slope of 0.4582 O2% by vol / g fuel, and the molecular weight for pmma of 100 g/gmol for the majority of the data, we can use the above equations to solve for the effective equivalence ratio for the tests: Φglobal = 1.3, which is fuel rich.
source_title: Results from On-Board CSA-CP and CDM Sensor Readings During the BASS-II Experiment in the MSG (ICES-2015-196)

objective: Study burning of a 2-cm acrylic (PMMA) sphere at reduced oxygen to compare flame growth, flame-to-fuel distance and regression rate with models.
key_finding: Reducing oxygen from 21% to 17% keeps the flame blue much longer (soot formation delayed), facilitating comparison with models.
quote: Flame sequence of a burning 2-cm diameter acrylic sphere at 17 percent oxygen and 12 cm/s flow from the Burning and Suppression of Solids experiment.
source_title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (ISS Researcher's Guide series)

objective: Burn a 2-cm acrylic sphere in microgravity at 17% oxygen with low flow.
key_finding: Vapor bubbles formed in the solid ignite as they burst through the blue flame, producing yellowish-red streaks.
quote: A snapshot of 2-cm diameter acrylic sphere burning in microgravity at 17 percent oxygen and 10 cm/s flow from the Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS) experiment conducted on the International Space Station.
source_title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (ISS Researcher's Guide series)

objective: Test flame burning in microgravity at ISS air conditions with airflow as the main variable.
fuel: PMMA spheres, flat samples, porous wax slabs, wax candles
key_finding: BASS results indicate NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative; materials can burn at lower oxygen levels in microgravity than on Earth.
quote: The glovebox is normally limited to ISS “air,” nominally 21 percent oxygen by volume and one atmospheric pressure.
source_title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (ISS Researcher's Guide series)

objective: Evaluate nitrogen gas as a local suppressant on burning samples in microgravity.
key_finding: Nitrogen applied locally can strengthen the flame by entraining oxygen; local suppressant jet sustains the flame even with ambient flow off.
quote: Early results have demonstrated that nitrogen applied to the flame can actually strengthen it because of this effect.
source_title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (ISS Researcher's Guide series)

objective: Examine how inert gas suppressant addition affects the flammability limit of heptane droplets.
key_finding: Flammability limit is lower in reduced gravity; terrestrial inert suppressant standards do not give the same safety margin in low gravity.
quote: Flame image of n-heptane droplet burning in 70 percent carbon dioxide, 21 percent oxygen, balance nitrogen and translated to the right at 3 cm/s.
source_title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (ISS Researcher's Guide series)

objective: Compare sooting propensity of ethanol droplets in different diluents.
key_finding: Sooting propensity differs among diluents.
quote: Comparison of sooting propensity in different diluents with ethanol burning in 30 percent oxygen at pressure of 2.4 atm.
source_title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (ISS Researcher's Guide series)

objective: Precursor test of a spherical ethylene diffusion flame on a porous burner for soot inception study.
key_finding: Spherical sooty flame established with 1.51 mg/s ethylene into quiescent air.
quote: The gas from the burner was 1.51 mg/s of 100 percent ethylene issuing into air at atmospheric pressure.
source_title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (ISS Researcher's Guide series)

objective: Precursor test of a partially premixed spherical flame on a porous burner.
key_finding: Partially premixed spherical flame achieved in microgravity.
quote: The gas issuing from the burner was 25 percent propane, 2 percent oxygen, 49 percent argon, and 24 percent nitrogen.
source_title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (ISS Researcher's Guide series)

objective: Show flame spread response to stepwise decreases in opposed flow over cotton-fiberglass fabric.
key_finding: Flame and spread rate respond rapidly and dramatically to flow changes from 10 cm/s to below 1 cm/s.
quote: The flow is decreased in discrete steps from 10 cm/s all the way down to less than 1 cm/s.
source_title: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (ISS Researcher's Guide series)

objective: Measure burning rate and extinction diameter of a free-floated methanol droplet burning in air at 1 atm (Run #204).
measurements: back-lit droplet camera, UV (OH*) flame camera, color camera
key_finding: D^2 versus time was fairly linear until just before extinction, with a diffusive extinction at a droplet diameter of 1.10 mm. The flame diameter grew and then shrank, so extinction was caused by insufficient residence time rather than radiation.
quote: Run #204 corresponds to a methanol droplet of initial diameter 2.75 mm burning in air (20% O2 and 79% N2) at one atmospheric pressure.
source_title: Methanol Droplet Combustion in Oxygen-Inert Environments in Microgravity

objective: Measure methanol droplet burning and extinction with CO2 diluent at 0.7 atm (Run #110).
measurements: back-lit droplet camera, UV (OH*) flame camera, color camera
key_finding: Diffusive extinction occurred at a diameter of 1.57 mm. The burning rate was lower than with He substitution. The droplet stayed in view after extinction and continued to evaporate slowly.
quote: Run #110 corresponds to a droplet with an initial diameter of 2.83 mm burning in 21%O2 and 30% CO2 environment
source_title: Methanol Droplet Combustion in Oxygen-Inert Environments in Microgravity

objective: Determine the limiting oxygen index of methanol droplets in O2-N2-CO2 and O2-N2-He mixtures, covering diffusive and radiative extinction.
sample_geometry: droplets of 1.5-4.5 mm initial diameter, free-floated or SiC-fiber tethered
measurements: back-lit droplet camera, UV (OH*) flame camera, color camera
key_finding: More than 100 droplets were burned at 0.7 and 1 atm with O2 from 30% down to 12%. The limiting oxygen index for methanol in these diluents is around 12-13% O2. Larger droplets at lower O2 extinguish radiatively, while smaller droplets extinguish diffusively.
quote: The experiments also show that the limiting oxygen index for methanol in these diluent gases is around 12% to 13% oxygen by volume.
source_title: Methanol Droplet Combustion in Oxygen-Inert Environments in Microgravity

objective: Examine how thermal and species fields diverge and lead to microgravity flame extinguishment by varying fuel thickness (residence time driven flame spread).
sample_geometry: thin sheets 1 cm and 2 cm wide, 0.1-0.4 mm thick
key_finding: Radiative quenching extinction occurs at low opposing flow (below ~2 cm/s) and blow-off extinction occurs near 40 cm/s for the 0.1 mm thick sample.
quote: Sequence of top views showing radiative quenching when flow velocity goes below 2 cm/s. Flame nearing blow off extinction as the flow velocity crosses 40 cm/s.
source_title: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment

objective: Understand the effect of space exploration atmospheres on ignition and flame spread of PMMA rods in low-speed flow.
key_finding: O2 range 16-21%, flow 0.4-4 cm/s, 54 unique spread rates. Spread rate decreases with increasing rod diameter, is lower in microgravity than in 1g, and increases with O2 in microgravity.
quote: Oxygen concentrations between 16% to 21% and flow velocity between 0.4 cm/sec to 4 cm/sec were tested. The total set of experiments yielded 54 unique flame spread rates.
source_title: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment

objective: Obtain microgravity opposed-flow flame spread data over thermally thick PMMA to compare with the 1-g Narrow Channel Apparatus.
sample_geometry: slabs 1 cm and 2 cm wide, 1-5 mm thick, one- and two-sided
key_finding: 20 test points, opposed flow with flow speed varied during each test. Initial O2 was 18-20% and dropped somewhat during tests (o2_percent is a midpoint of that range).
quote: The initial oxygen level varied between 18% and 20%, but dropped somewhat during each test.
source_title: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment

objective: Map the microgravity flammability boundary of PMMA rods in concurrent (stagnation point) flow to find the minimum oxygen concentration.
key_finding: Steady spreading was obtained at 13.6% O2 in BASS-II versus a 1g blowoff limit of 16%, giving a negative oxygen margin of safety of 2.4% O2. 24 rods were burned.
quote: The 1g blowoff for the ¼” rod is at 16% oxygen, whereas we obtained steady spreading at 13.6% oxygen in BASS-II.
source_title: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment

objective: Determine flame growth and extinction characteristics of thin SIBAL fabric in purely forced concurrent flow in zero gravity at varied O2.
sample_geometry: fabric strips 1.2 cm or 2.2 cm wide, 10 cm long
key_finding: Quenching extinction demonstrated as flow was reduced from 5 to 2.2 cm/s for a 2.2-cm wide sample; 6 quenching cases and 1 blow-off case overall; steady spread with a limiting flame length observed.
quote: Top view of a typical quenching time sequence. 2.2-cm wide SIBAL fabric sample in 1 atm. and 18.7% O2. Ignited at 5 cm/s flow at right end, then reduced to 2.2 cm/s gradually.
source_title: Combustion of Solids in Microgravity: Results from the BASS-II Experiment

objective: Measure fire growth, heat release and combustion products from a SIBAL fabric sample in low-g with concurrent flow in an exploration atmosphere.
measurements: oxygen consumption calorimetry, fuel consumption calorimetry, temperature, CO/CO2 sensors, far-field diagnostics
key_finding: Burn duration 112 s, peak heat release 3217 W, FFD inlet CO2 increase 2800 ppm and CO increase 120 ppm.
source_title: Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment (ICES 2024)

objective: Characterize fire growth, heat release and hazardous gas/smoke generation for a thick two-sided PMMA sample in low-g.
sample_geometry: 1 cm thick two-sided PMMA, 18 cm long
measurements: oxygen consumption calorimetry, radiometer, temperature sensors, CO/CO2 sensors, ion chamber and particulate monitors
key_finding: Ignition at 637 s, burn 780 s, peak heat release 3080 W; flow reduced to 5 cm/s at 1120 s and terminated at 1420 s. CO and CO2 exceeded 24-hour CO and 1-hour CO2 limits; smoke detected at 981 s.
quote: Ignition at 637 s Flow was changed from 20 cm/s to 5 cm/s at 1120 seconds
source_title: Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment (ICES 2024)

objective: Characterize burning of a thick one-sided PMMA sample in low-g and its effect on cabin atmosphere.
sample_geometry: 0.5 cm thick one-sided PMMA, 18 cm long
measurements: oxygen consumption calorimetry, temperature, CO/CO2 sensors, far-field diagnostics
key_finding: Burn duration 1200 s, peak heat release 1507 W, FFD inlet CO2 increase 8117 ppm and CO increase 320 ppm.
source_title: Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment (ICES 2024)

objective: Characterize the morphology and size distribution of smoke particles from overheated Kapton, fresh and aged.
measurements: particle size distribution (geometric mean, arithmetic mean, mass-average diameter, geometric std dev)
key_finding: Fresh Kapton smoke had a geometric mean diameter of 47 nm, an arithmetic mean of 62 nm, a mass-average diameter of 106 nm and σg of 2.07. Aged smoke grew to 102, 121 and 169 nm, with σg 1.79.
source_title: Particle Morphology Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight

objective: Characterize the morphology and size distribution of smoke particles from overheated lamp wick, fresh and aged.
measurements: particle size distribution (geometric mean, arithmetic mean, mass-average diameter, geometric std dev)
key_finding: Fresh lamp wick smoke had a geometric mean diameter of 103 nm, an arithmetic mean of 142 nm, a mass-average diameter of 271 nm and σg of 2.23. Aged smoke grew to 269, 308 and 401 nm, with σg 1.67.
source_title: Particle Morphology Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight

objective: Characterize the morphology and size distribution of smoke particles from overheated silicone, fresh and aged.
measurements: particle size distribution (geometric mean, arithmetic mean, mass-average diameter, geometric std dev)
key_finding: Fresh silicone smoke had a geometric mean diameter of 152 nm, an arithmetic mean of 221 nm, a mass-average diameter of 468 nm and σg of 2.38. Aged smoke grew to 320, 400 and 628 nm, with σg 1.96.
source_title: Particle Morphology Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight

objective: Characterize the morphology and size distribution of smoke particles from overheated Teflon, fresh and aged.
measurements: particle size distribution (geometric mean, arithmetic mean, mass-average diameter, geometric std dev)
key_finding: Fresh Teflon smoke had a geometric mean diameter of 93 nm, an arithmetic mean of 111 nm, a mass-average diameter of 173 nm and σg of 2.08. Aged smoke measured 80, 115 and 237 nm, with σg 2.34. Aging did not increase the geometric mean diameter.
source_title: Particle Morphology Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight

objective: Characterize the morphology and size distribution of smoke particles from overheated Pyrell foam, fresh and aged.
measurements: particle size distribution (geometric mean, arithmetic mean, mass-average diameter, geometric std dev)
key_finding: Fresh Pyrell smoke had a geometric mean diameter of 177 nm, an arithmetic mean of 227 nm, a mass-average diameter of 377 nm and σg of 2.03. Aged smoke grew to 348, 400 and 529 nm, with σg 1.70.
source_title: Particle Morphology Results from the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight

objective: Assess flame spread of a large-scale fire in microgravity (spread rate, mass consumption, heat release).
sample_geometry: 40.6 cm wide x 0.37 mm thick, 94 cm length, concurrent-flow
key_finding: A steady flame was achieved even for a wide sample in concurrent flow; it burned about 84 cm in microgravity over 420 s at 1.8 mm/s. In 1-g the same sample burned completely with accelerating spread.
quote: The average concurrent-flow flame spread rate is 1.8 mm/s.
source_title: Results of Large-Scale Spacecraft Flammability Tests

objective: Measure opposed-flow flame spread on the remaining wide fabric sample after the concurrent test.
sample_geometry: 40.6 cm wide x 0.37 mm thick, ~10 cm of fuel remaining, opposed-flow
key_finding: The opposed flame was shorter (24 mm) than the concurrent flame (~40 mm) and spread at 1.3 mm/s. It burned about 70 s.
quote: The opposed-flow flame average spread rate 1.3 mm/s.
source_title: Results of Large-Scale Spacecraft Flammability Tests

objective: Verify flammability limits of materials in low gravity, comparing against 1-g results.
sample_geometry: 5 cm wide x 0.37 mm thick, 29 cm length, concurrent-flow
key_finding: The 5 cm sample burned its full 29 cm length in 145 s, marginally faster than the 40.6 cm wide sample (2.1 vs 1.8 mm/s). The authors attribute this partly to higher O2 and possibly side entrainment.
quote: The flame spread rate for the 5-cm-wide sample is marginally faster compared to the spread rate for the 40.6-cm-wide sample for the same flow speed of 20 cm/s (2.1 compared to 1.8 mm/s).
source_title: Results of Large-Scale Spacecraft Flammability Tests

objective: Measure fabric flame spread at a higher flow speed of 25 cm/s.
sample_geometry: 5 cm wide x 0.37 mm thick, 29 cm length, concurrent-flow
key_finding: The flame consumed the full 29 cm in 115 s at 2.6 mm/s, faster than at 20 cm/s.
quote: | 2 6 - | | 80 W | 9 2 s . | 115 s | | 29 cm | 2 6 mm/ s . | Complete | Acceleratory |
source_title: Results of Large-Scale Spacecraft Flammability Tests

objective: Test silicone flammability in microgravity across thicknesses, in concurrent and opposed flow.
sample_geometry: 5 cm wide, 0.27, 0.61 and 1.03 mm thick concurrent samples, 0.37 mm opposed sample, 29 cm length
key_finding: None of the silicone samples burned in microgravity. A tiny flame persisted after the igniter was turned off but did not spread. In 1-g, the thin sample burned completely, so silicone flammability appears reduced in microgravity.
quote: Results were convincing although rather anticlimactic as none of the silicone samples burned.
source_title: Results of Large-Scale Spacecraft Flammability Tests

objective: Test whether Nomex ignites when exposed to a PMMA pilot flame.
sample_geometry: 5 cm wide, PMMA 0.85 mm and Nomex 0.37 mm thick, concurrent-flow
key_finding: Nomex could not be ignited even when bathed by a pilot flame (burn duration 140 s).
quote: Nomex®, a common material used on the ISS and rated “safe,” could not be ignited even when bathed by a pilot flame.
source_title: Results of Large-Scale Spacecraft Flammability Tests

objective: Test thick PMMA flammability in microgravity using stronger, longer ignition.
sample_geometry: 5 cm wide, thick samples (2-8 variable cross-section, 2-9 1 cm thick), 29 cm length
key_finding: Samples 2-8 and 2-9 burned for 600 s and 900 s, with a microgravity burn length of ~10 cm. A spread rate is not given in the table (Note iv). In 1-g they burned completely.
quote: Samples 2-8 and 2-9 had slightly more powerful igniters (97 W instead of 80 W) and were left on longer (30 s instead of 9.2 s) to assure ignition of these thick fuels.
source_title: Results of Large-Scale Spacecraft Flammability Tests

objective: Observe concurrent flame growth and spread over a large thin SIBAL fabric sample in a reduced-height duct.
sample_geometry: 40 cm wide x 50 cm long fabric
measurements: video, radiometers, thermocouples, gas sensors (O2, CO2, CO) at inlet and outlet, remote CO2/temperature sensors
key_finding: Flame reached a steady size of 8.5 cm (max 11.0 cm) in the 30 cm duct. The spread rate roughly doubled compared with the larger duct of Saffire I and III.
quote: Flight/Sample IV-1 IV-2 V-2 V-3 V-4 Material/configuration SIBAL Cloth 2-sided PMMA Cotton Jersey 1 sided PMMA Structured PMMA Length (cm) 50 18 50 18 20 Air Flow Rate (cm/s) 20 20 20 20 20
source_title: Fire Safety Implications of Preliminary Results from Saffire IV and V Experiments on Large Scale Spacecraft Fires (ICES-2021-266)

objective: Study concurrent flame growth and extinguishment on a two-sided thick PMMA slab in air, including reduced and zero flow.
sample_geometry: 2-sided slab, 10 mm thick, 18 cm long, 40 cm wide
key_finding: Flame was pinned to the leading edge and grew to 9.5 cm after 400 s. Bubbling fuel jets kept the flame alive through 15 s of no flow. A deflagration occurred at 5 cm/s, and soot later blocked the outlet screens.
quote: For Saffire IV-2, the two-sided PMMA sample flame burning in air grew to 9.5 cm after 400 seconds.
source_title: Fire Safety Implications of Preliminary Results from Saffire IV and V Experiments on Large Scale Spacecraft Fires (ICES-2021-266)

objective: Observe concurrent flame spread over a thin cotton jersey fabric in elevated O2 and reduced pressure, and test delayed extinguishment.
sample_geometry: 40 cm wide x 50 cm long fabric, 18.1 mg/cm2
measurements: video, surface thermocouples, radiometer, gas sensors
key_finding: Flame reached a steady size of 10.0 cm (max 14.0 cm). The flame regrew after a 70 s fan-off interval, showing thin fuels can burn on without forced flow. Curled char later disturbed the flow over sample V-4.
quote: Despite this long interval, the flame grew back when the flow was turned on again and continued to burn for another 150 seconds until the material was consumed.
source_title: Fire Safety Implications of Preliminary Results from Saffire IV and V Experiments on Large Scale Spacecraft Fires (ICES-2021-266)

objective: Test whether extended reduced flow (5 cm/s) promotes rapid extinguishment of a one-sided PMMA flame.
sample_geometry: 1-sided slab, 5 mm thick, 18 cm long, 40 cm wide
key_finding: Flame was pinned at the leading edge and grew to 11 cm after 450 s. After 300 s at 5 cm/s the flame extinguished immediately when the fan was turned off.
quote: In Saffire V-3, the one-sided PMMA sample flame (in 25.4% oxygen) grew to 11 cm after 450 seconds.
source_title: Fire Safety Implications of Preliminary Results from Saffire IV and V Experiments on Large Scale Spacecraft Fires (ICES-2021-266)

objective: Study opposed flame spread over a structured (ribbed) PMMA sample and the ignition deflagration.
sample_geometry: structured slab, 10 mm thick, 20 cm long, 3 mm high ribs 1-10 mm wide, 2 cm between rib faces
measurements: top and edge view video, radiometer
key_finding: Spread was faster on thinner ribs, so rib width was the relevant sample dimension. A strong deflagration occurred at ignition, and downstream sample V-3 was ignited but extinguished by the oxygen shadow of the upstream flame.
quote: The flame spread more rapidly on the thin ribs at the top of the image with decreasing spread rate as the ribs become wider.
source_title: Fire Safety Implications of Preliminary Results from Saffire IV and V Experiments on Large Scale Spacecraft Fires (ICES-2021-266)

objective: Assess concurrent flame spread over a large-scale cotton-fiberglass sample in microgravity.
sample_geometry: 40.6 cm wide x 0.37 mm thick x 94 cm long
key_finding: Concurrent flame spread covered about 84 cm in a 420 s burn at 1.8 mm/s. The same sample in 1-g burned completely with accelerating spread. O2 fell from 21.7 to 21.5% during the test.
quote: | 1 1 - | 182 W | 8 s | 420 s | ~ 84 cm | 1 8 mm/ s . | Compl ete | Accel eratory |
source_title: Saffire: A Novel Approach to Study of Spacecraft Fire Safety Using Un-manned Spacecraft

objective: Assess opposed-flow flame spread over cotton-fiberglass in microgravity.
sample_geometry: 40.6 cm wide x 0.37 mm thick x ~10 cm long
key_finding: Opposed-flow spread burned about 10 cm in 70 s at 1.3 mm/s. The same sample in 1-g did not spread (~0 burn length).
source_title: Saffire: A Novel Approach to Study of Spacecraft Fire Safety Using Un-manned Spacecraft

objective: Test flammability of silicone sheets of different thickness (0.27, 0.61, 1.03 mm) in concurrent flow in microgravity.
sample_geometry: 5 cm wide x 29 cm long, thickness 0.27, 0.61 or 1.03 mm
key_finding: All three silicone thicknesses had an insignificant burn in microgravity (~0 burn length). In 1-g the 0.27 mm sample burned completely with accelerating spread, the 0.61 mm sample burned 7.6 cm at 1.2 mm/s, and the 1.03 mm sample did not spread.

objective: Determine the radiative extinction (critical opposed-flow) velocity for thin PMMA in microgravity by gradually reducing the flow.
sample_geometry: 100 um thick, 20 mm wide, ~95 mm long sheet
measurements: color still camera, video, radiometer, hot-wire anemometer flow calibration
key_finding: Steady spread of 2.2 mm/s was established; with flow gradually reduced from 3 cm/s the flame radiatively extinguished at about 1.1 cm/s.
quote: After the flame propagated across half the sample length at a steady spread rate of 2.2 mm/s, the flow was abruptly cut off and the flame was observed to extinguish within 2 s.
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Test whether the radiative extinction velocity depends on fuel thickness at ambient O2.
key_finding: Extinction velocity was about 1 cm/s for 100, 200, 300 um and about 1.5 cm/s for 400 um, i.e. independent of fuel thickness.
quote: When tests are repeated with samples of different thicknesses, the extinction velocities are found to be about 1 cm/s for 100, 200, and 300 μm and about 1.5 cm/s for 400 μm.
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Determine the extinction velocity at reduced O2 for thin PMMA.
sample_geometry: 100 um (20 mm wide) and 200 um (10 mm wide) sheets
key_finding: Extinction velocity rose to about 2.6 cm/s (100 um) and about 4 cm/s (200 um) at ~16% O2, so it increases significantly as O2 decreases.
quote: Tests were also conducted at a lower O2 level of about 16 percent for two different thicknesses and the extinction velocities were found to be about 2.6 cm/s for 100 μm and about 4 cm/s for 200 μm.
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Determine flame spread rate and compare thermal regime in microgravity with downward 1g spread over thin PMMA.
measurements: top-view still camera, side video, flame analyzer image processing
key_finding: The highest microgravity spread rate (2.2 mm/s) matches the 1g downward spread rate (2.0 mm/s), indicating downward spread at 21% O2 is thermally controlled.
quote: For the same fuel thickness, the highest spread rate obtained is about 2.2 mm/s even though the opposing flow velocity was varied from
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Provide normal-gravity downward spread reference data for PMMA to compare against microgravity results.
key_finding: Average downward spread rate was steady at 2.0 mm/s.
quote: The average spread rate over the 100-μm-thick sample in the normal-gravity experiments is found to be 2.0 mm/s (see Figure 2.19(b)).
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Establish the thick-limit downward spread rate for PMMA.
key_finding: Thick-limit downward spread rate averaged 0.044 mm/s; effective buoyant opposing flow estimated at 1.9 cm/s.
quote: an average value of 0.044 mm/s is selected as the average spread rate for downward spread over PMMA in the thick limit.
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Evaluate the flammability of Nomex, which is used as a fire barrier aboard the ISS.

source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Burn a leftover BASS-I wax candle in opposed flow at several flow velocities.

quote: The wax candle test successfully ignited in an opposed flow (akin to holding a candle upside down) and burned at five different flow velocities corresponding to the test matrix potentiometer settings as shown in Figure 3.1.
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Find the minimum O2 for opposed-flow flame spread over black PMMA rods in microgravity and compare it with 1g.
key_finding: Flame spread was seen down to 17.5% O2 in microgravity but not below 19% in 1g. Spread was faster in microgravity than in 1g and increased as rod diameter decreased.

source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Find the lowest-O2 quenching limit for concurrent flame over a PMMA rod in stagnation flow.
sample_geometry: rod radius 0.476 cm with hemispherical tip
measurements: color video, still camera, radiometer, O2/CO2/CO sensors
key_finding: Initial O2 was 14.8% and final 13.6%. Rod regression reached a steady 0.0385 mm/s. Radiometer oscillations at about 1.1 Hz preceded quenching extinction.
quote: Figure 6.4 shows a detailed time history of flame measurements (flame length, width, standoff distance, aspect ratio, rod tip position, and radiometer reading) of the lowest O2 quenching test, where the initial O2 setting was 14.8 percent O2 (by volume) and the final O2 reading was 13.6 percent O2.
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Determine the ignition limit and ignition delay of PMMA rods versus O2.
key_finding: Sustained ignition was not possible below about 14.5% initial O2. Ignition delay rose sharply below 16% and reached up to 230 s for larger rods. Flames ignited at higher O2 survived down to 13.6% O2.
quote: Below an initial O2 concentration of ~14.5 percent O2, a sustained ignition could not be achieved even though flames were observed when the igniter was on and briefly after the igniter was turned off before extinguishing.
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Observe a local blowoff and attempted re-establishment of the stagnation flame on a PMMA rod.
key_finding: A flame hole of 9–10 mm formed at blowoff. The flame was re-established only once; on the second attempt it blew off completely. This shows the flame cannot repropagate upstream at low O2.
quote: This second blowoff is interpreted as indicating that once the flame is stabilized farther than the thermal length downstream of the stagnation region (ℓ = 2 mm), the flame is unable to repropagate upstream for the low O2 levels tested (XO2 final = 14.5 percent for this test) even though the fuel is already preheated.
source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)

objective: Build the O2-stretch flammability boundary for PMMA rods in concurrent flow.

source_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report (NASA/TM-20210011385)
